takeaways.label: Strong H1, 42% revenue growth
takeaways.text: Q2 revenue grew 41.9% YoY, with ~85% of the increase coming from volume and the rest from price realization, while PAT rose 51.8% on operating leverage and a richer product mix.

takeaways.label: Value-added mix hits 75%
takeaways.text: Stearin and other value-added products now contribute ~75% of total sales volume, up from 65% previously, driving margin expansion even as freight costs rose.

takeaways.label: Inventory spike is seasonal, not structural
takeaways.text: Inventory jumped to ₹1,000 crore from ₹728 crore in March because shea procurement started earlier this year alongside sal and mango seed buying; management expects normalization in H2.

takeaways.label: New capacity still 18 months from commissioning
takeaways.text: The next fractionation plant is expected online around Q3–Q4 FY28, with a gradual ramp from 40–50% utilization toward 85–90% over 2–3 years, meaning meaningful volume contribution only from FY29.

watch.label: What to watch next quarter
watch.text: Whether elevated inventory normalizes as promised, the pace of remaining debottlenecking completion by year-end, and any update on Burkina Faso regulatory approvals for the backward integration project.

points.label: Volumes drove the quarter
points.text: ~85% of YoY revenue growth came from volume, with 10–15% from price realization, reflecting strong underlying demand rather than commodity tailwinds.

points.label: Products are supply-constrained
points.text: Management stated that CBE and specialty fats are "short in supply" and capacities are "quite booked for the near term," with no slowdown visible in demand.

points.label: Customer growth is broad-based
points.text: Growth came from a mixture of new customers in new geographies and higher uptake from existing customers, though the exact split was not disclosed.

points.label: Receivables spike was timing, not stress
points.text: The increase in receivables was due to the last 15 days of September revenue; remittance was already received and the cycle normalized to the usual 30 days.

quotes.text: Ashok Kumar Jain: "The product, uh, what we are manufacturing currently are short in supply only. So we are not seeing any slowdown with respect to demand for our product portfolio. The demands are very healthy currently. Our capacities are also quite booked for the next kind of..."

points.label: Value-added contribution reached ~75%
points.text: Stearin and other value-added products now account for ~75% of total sales volume, up from 65% then 70% in prior periods, driven by product mix upgrades.

points.label: EBITDA margin band is stable
points.text: Management sees the current 25–27% EBITDA margin band as comfortable, with modest quarter-to-quarter movements possible due to macroeconomic factors.

points.label: Freight costs are the margin headwind
points.text: Raw material cost elevation is at the gross profit level, driven by freight cost increases from global macro events, fuel price hikes, and transportation cost escalation; management declined to quantify the percentage increase on the call.

points.label: CBE pricing is not linked to cocoa
points.text: Management explicitly stated that CBE and stearin pricing has no direct linkage to cocoa price movements; recent contract renewals are getting cost-margin benefits and prices are in a stable mode.

points.label: New capacity should lift margins gradually
points.text: Margins are expected to improve as new capacities ramp up, driven by product mix changes, operating leverage, and economies of scale.

quotes.text: Ashok Kumar Jain: "It's not that there will be impact just because CBE prices are falling. So the thing we want to clear is on that, that there is no linkage that way when one commodity prices moves for cocoa to that of our products of shea and mango."

points.label: Existing plant running at 85%
points.text: The expanded 47,500-ton capacity is operating at ~85% utilization, with debottlenecking completed last quarter enabling an 85–90% range.

points.label: Remaining debottlenecking by FY27-end
points.text: The second unit's debottlenecking is expected to be completed by the end of this financial year, adding further headroom.

points.label: New fractionation capacity timeline
points.text: Commissioning expected around Q3–Q4 FY28, with utilization starting at 40–50% and taking 2–3 years to reach the optimum 85–90%, meaning FY29 is when more meaningful contribution begins.

points.label: Growth headroom is multi-layered
points.text: Headroom exists from unutilized capacity, remaining debottlenecking, and a 5–10% price benefit from inflation and other factors for FY27 and FY28.

points.label: Asset turnover direction
points.text: On optimum utilization, management directionally expects around 5–7x asset turnover from investments, depending on product mix.

points.label: Burkina Faso land acquired, approvals pending
points.text: Land has been acquired for the backward integration project; regulatory approvals are awaited, with project completion expected around Q3–Q4 FY28.

points.label: Backward integration cost advantage
points.text: Management sees a 2–3% cost advantage from the Africa backward integration; too early to comment on exact financial impact, but it should benefit raw material sourcing over the longer term.

points.label: CapEx spending back-half loaded
points.text: A larger chunk of investment is expected in H2 FY27 or the coming fiscal year, after design and engineering completion.

points.label: Solvent fractionation plant in planning
points.text: Currently in the planning and engineering stage; described as a complex project due to varying yields across wild crops and raw materials, with updates promised only "once something substantially materialized."

points.label: LATAM facility ramping gradually
points.text: Expected to ramp up over the next few quarters or about a year; currently fully booked on existing capacity with product going from the Indian plant to the Latin plant for rework.

points.label: Leadership restructured for scale
points.text: Mr. Mudit Kumar Singh appointed as Chairman for governance and risk oversight; Mr. Deep Saraf elevated to Managing Director to run operations, manufacturing, supply chain, and project delivery; Mrs. Vineeta Saraf appointed President Business Excellence and Development; Mr. Ashish Saraf moved to President, Strategic Planning and Business Development to focus on long-term strategy, global partnerships, and new growth opportunities.

points.label: Rationale is organizational maturity
points.text: Management framed the change as necessary because quarterly revenue is now above ₹400 crore, exports are 61% of revenue, and the company serves customers in more than 39 countries, requiring dedicated leadership for each part of the business.

points.label: Strategy and culture unchanged
points.text: Mr. Ashish Saraf assured that strategies, values, and culture remain exactly the same, with customers and suppliers continuing to work with the same team; what improves is clarity, speed of decision-making, and accountability.

points.label: Team expanded for complex projects
points.text: The company has recruited nationals and international experts to contribute expertise for upcoming complex projects.

quotes.text: Ashish Saraf: "Manorama today is a very different company from the one we were a few years ago. Our quarterly revenue is now above Rs 400 crores. We serve customers in more than 39 countries with exports at 61% of revenue. We have strengthened our balance sheet and we are about to go for major expansions going forward. A company at this stage deserves dedicated leadership for each part of the business rather than one team carrying every responsibility."

items.title: Debottlenecking to 52,000 TPA
items.text: SF2 was debottlenecked 30% to 32,500 MTPA, taking fractionation capacity to 47,500 MTPA, with the remaining ~4,500-ton MDP debottlenecking under planning as of Q2 FY27 and expected around Q3 FY27 for ₹8-10 crore. Management guides ~30% volume growth plus 5-10% price realization in FY27, with 40-45% growth available over 1-2 years from debottlenecked capacity and ~15% utilisation headroom.

items.title: ₹460 crore CBA/ESOS forward integration
items.text: Board-approved ₹460 crore program covering a 75,000 MT CBA/ESOS plant, 75,000 MT solvent fractionation (SF3) and 90,000 MT refinery, with ₹70 crore spent by Q2 FY27, FY27 spend guided at ₹225-250 crore and commissioning targeted around Q3 FY28. Funded by internal accruals plus a completed ₹499.99 crore QIP (2 Jul 2026), it targets >5x asset turnover at current ~25-27% EBITDA margins, with volume contribution from Q4 FY28/FY29.

items.title: Burkina Faso shea crushing
items.text: A ~90,000 MTPA shea/mango processing factory (~₹120-130 crore) is underway with land purchased, an MoU with the Government of Burkina Faso signed, subsidiary Taang Kaam operationalised, and timeline guided to Q3-Q4 FY28. Crushing at origin shifts freight from seeds to butter (~45-60% of raw material weight), improving yield and adding an expected ~2-3% cost advantage with ~3-year payback.

items.title: Brazil/LATAM Dekel partnership
items.text: The Dekel Agroindustria processing arrangement in Brazil delivered its first commercial CBE/specialty fats batch in FY26, with trial production from Jun 2026 and revenue already starting at minor contribution. Ramp-up is expected over the next 2-4 quarters, opening a large consumption market beyond the top 5-6 global customers at a per-ton processing cost with no upfront payment.

items.title: Premiumising the product mix
items.text: Value-added products (stearin and CBE) reached ~75% of sales volume by Q2 FY27, with management targeting 70-80% of sales over time and CBE rising from ~10% of revenue two years ago to ~30% in FY26. The shift drove FY26 EBITDA margin expansion of 230 bps to 27.1%, and management expects further structural improvement over 2-3 years as new capacity ramps.

items.title: Africa sourcing network deepening
items.text: A new sourcing subsidiary in Chad was incorporated on 20 Jul 2026, and the Board approved share-capital increases across Ghana, Nigeria, Burkina, Chad and UAE units on 4 Sep 2026 to strengthen international operations. With subsidiaries across 10 African regions and shea procurement already under way in FY27, this secures raw material for the debottlenecked and new capacity coming online.
